span.label: **THE ASYMMETRY IS STATED AS SETTLED BACKGROUND, AND THREE YEARS LATER IT IS AN ARTEFACT.** `Quotation withheld` Written as review, not as a claim under test - which is what makes it worth tagging. **lukatela2007 minimised study-test asymmetries across five experiments and found EQUAL magnitudes**, with the conventional advantage returning only in a within-subjects design. Kirsner1986 reasons from the asymmetry; this record goes looking for its brain basis; lukatela2007 dissolves it. **Three records, one day, none citing the others**
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE NEURAL RESULT IS A DISSOCIATION IN DIRECTION, NOT JUST IN LOCATION:** cross-modal priming gave a larger rCBF DECREASE in left inferior temporal and fusiform cortex - regions tied to modality-independent lexical retrieval - while `WITHIN-MODALITY auditory priming was associated with a bilateral pattern of prefrontal rCBF INCREASE.` Different regions and opposite signs. **Whatever the behavioural asymmetry turns out to be, these two conditions are not one process running at two strengths in this data** - which is a constraint that survives even if lukatela2007 is right that the behavioural difference is a design artefact
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE DEFINITION PUTS THE CRITERION IN THE INSTRUCTIONS, WHICH IS EASY TO READ PAST:** repetition priming manifests as facilitation or a completion bias `WHEN TEST INSTRUCTIONS DO NOT MAKE ANY REFERENCE TO PRIOR EVENTS.` Not `when the subject is unaware`, not `when memory is not consciously used` - **when the experimenter did not mention it.** The construct is operationalised by what was said to the participant, and the 90%% discussion of this same paper concedes that `involuntary conscious memory` may occur anyway when the study context is reinstated. The definition and the caveat are in the same paper
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: repetition priming —is-a→ implicit memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **THE CLEANEST `is-a` I HAVE CUT THIS SESSION, AND THEY ARE RARE.** `Repetition priming IS A FORM OF implicit memory` - the relation is the sentence's main verb, both endpoints are named as words, and there is no hedge to preserve. Weight 0.95. Most taxonomy in this literature has to be inferred from how terms are used together; here it is asserted directly, in an introduction, as the thing the reader is expected to already accept.

span.label: within-modality —operationalised-as→ modality
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — **WEAK ON PURPOSE, AND THE WEAKNESS IS WHERE THE SPAN STOPS.** The quote names the condition and its neural correlate; it does not define what `within-modality` means. That definition is in the methods, in a sentence carrying stereotactic coordinates that the table guard refuses. Weight 0.85 and the confidence at 0.95 only because the endpoint attestation is exact - `within-modality` is a word of this span and `modality` is inside it as a word too. **A reader taking this triple alone learns that the two are related and not how**, which the note has to say out loud.

span.label: Auditory-to-visual cross-modality priming produced a significantly larger blood-flow decrease at the left inferior temporal/fusiform boundary than within-modality auditory priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The interaction analysis confirmed the deactivation difference was specific to the cross-modality condition in left BA 37/20.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Within-modality auditory priming was accompanied by bilateral prefrontal blood-flow increases rather than posterior deactivations.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Right middle frontal activation was significantly greater for within-modality than for cross-modality priming, the reverse of what earlier studies had reported.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Behaviourally the within- and cross-modality priming effects did not differ in size, contrary to the usual finding of a within-modality advantage.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The magnitude of the left inferior temporal deactivation tracked each subject's behavioural cross-modality priming, tying the imaging effect to behaviour.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: No blood-flow decreases reached the conventional threshold for within-modality auditory priming, unlike previous auditory stem-completion PET reports.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming magnitude did not grow across successive study-test blocks, arguing against subjects adopting explicit retrieval strategies.
